title: Renewable energy
examples: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy sources?
Can wind turbines power a whole city?
Are there any disadvantages to using geothermal energy?

explain.say: Today we learn about renewable energy sources.

items: Solar energy comes from the sun.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a wind turbine. Look at the blades, the hub and the gearbox. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Solar power captures energy from sunlight using panels.
Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of wind into electricity.
Hydroelectric power generates electricity by moving water through turbines.

items: Turbine: Spins with the water force

explain.say: Geothermal energy taps into the heat naturally stored beneath the Earth's surface.

items: Power Plant: Uses the heat source

explain.say: For everyday use, solar panels on a house can power lights at night.

faq.q: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy?
faq.a: Renewable sources naturally replenish over a short time. Non-renewable sources take millions of years to form.
asks: Are solar and fossil fuels the same?
What is the difference between clean and dirty energy?

faq.q: Do wind turbines make noise when they are operating?
faq.a: Some people find that wind turbines can create some noise. This is sometimes a concern for people living nearby.
asks: What are the sound issues with wind farms?

faq.q: Are there any environmental problems with building dams for hydro power?
faq.a: Yes, building large dams can affect the river's natural flow and wildlife habitats. Fish migration can be impacted.
asks: What are the downsides of large dams?

faq.q: Is geothermal energy available everywhere on Earth?
faq.a: No, geothermal energy is best where hot water or steam is close to the surface. This limits where it can be used easily.
asks: Can I use geothermal energy in cold places?
Does every country have geothermal power?

faq.q: What is the main disadvantage of solar power?
faq.a: Solar panels only generate electricity when the sun is shining brightly. They do not work well at night.
asks: Does solar power work at night?

facts: Solar energy converts sunlight directly into electricity.
Wind turbines use large blades to capture the force of moving air.
Hydroelectric dams control the flow of rivers to generate power.
Geothermal power uses heat from inside the Earth's crust.

quiz.say: Which energy source relies on the heat from inside the Earth?
quiz.why: Geothermal energy directly uses heat stored within the Earth.

wrong.0: Solar power requires the energy source to be sunlight.
wrong.2: Wind energy comes from the movement of air, not internal heat.
wrong.3: Hydro power depends on the movement of surface water.

quiz.say: If a power source needs constant sunlight to work, it is most likely:
quiz.why: Solar power is directly dependent on the presence of the sun.

wrong.0: Hydro power relies on water flow, not just sunlight.
wrong.1: Geothermal power comes from underground heat, always available.
wrong.3: Wind power works even when the sun is not shining.

quiz.say: Which pair of energy sources are both considered renewable?
quiz.why: Both wind and solar energy are naturally replenished, making them renewable.

wrong.0: Oil and gas are also non-renewable resources we use up.
wrong.1: While biomass is renewable, coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
wrong.3: Fossil fuels are non-renewable resources that take millions of years to form.
